clause_results.text: In-hand slippage: while a part is held, it must not move relative to the gripper before it is released.

payload.explanation: relative_frame monitor mon_45e37930b2e9 (tcp vs line_green, armed at grasp close with reference translation 0.07602m) fired at trigger_wall_ns 1793658990798011400 with triggering_value 0.02024 against threshold 0.02 (departure from the armed reference distance). I pulled get_evidence over 1793658988.0e9-1793658992.5e9 on object_poses(line_green) and frames(tcp) to characterize it rather than report the raw crossing. The object's z position descended in step with the TCP until about wall_ns 1793658989897609200, then plateaued at z~0.0744 even as the TCP continued descending through z~0.128 by 1793658992497386200 -- the two stopped moving together. Over the same window line_green's orientation rotated roughly 25 degrees (quaternion x-component moving from about -0.008 to -0.22) while the TCP's own orientation stayed essentially fixed. This is not a mis-arming: the monitor measures translation only, and the translation drift it caught (reference 0.076m closing to about 0.056m, a 0.020m departure) is corroborated independently by the pose evidence showing the object's motion decoupling from the gripper's. The physical mechanism is a grasp slip during final insertion: line_green met resistance (most likely descending into or against the base1 fixture/slot) and rotated and settled in the gripper's jaws before release, rather than tracking the commanded TCP motion rigidly as pick_line_green's grasp (effort 10.86, width 0.0258 at closure) had established. I did not dismiss this as settling-after-release because release_skill had not yet been invoked at trigger time (it starts later, after this move_grasp_center_to_pose skill_end) -- the part was still nominally held. Capturing frames over the same window for the record (capture label line_green_slip_fire). No other object's stationarity monitor fired in this window (base1, u_brown, u_orange all remained silent), so this is isolated to the held part, not a bystander disturbance or dropped-part-strikes-neighbor event.

payload.explanation: At end_step the executor itself reported claimed_outcome=failure with position_error_m=0.0219 (tolerance 0.015) and orientation_error_deg=25 (tolerance 10), and I independently confirmed via query_snapshot: line_green at (0.40358,-0.19724,0.07424) vs line_green_placement (0.40413,-0.19878,0.05238), distance 0.0219m, well outside raw_spec.tolerances.position_m=0.015 for line_green, and orientation likewise far outside orientation_deg=10. This is the direct consequence of the in-hand slip already recorded for this step: the part rotated ~25 degrees and separated from the gripper's commanded path during final insertion (mon_45e37930b2e9 fire, trigger_wall_ns 1793658990798011400), so it was never actually driven down into the placement frame -- it settled high and tilted, then was released there. The executor's own notes ('did not seat... tipped ~25deg') agree with my independent measurement, so there is no disagreement to resolve here, only confirmation. u_brown and u_orange disturbance figures reported by the executor (0.00073m, 0.00064m) are consistent with no bystander/neighbor-part violation from this failure. The executor states it is attempting an unplanned recovery (re-grasp and reseat), which I will evaluate against the same placement frame and tolerance when it closes.

payload.explanation: Three stationarity monitors (mon_45c92dd02383 on base1, mon_fca6bae0bf67 on u_brown, mon_b1b17e87c7a5 on u_orange) fired within 1ms of each other at trigger_wall_ns ~1793659132948-949e9, each just over its 0.02m epsilon (0.0238, 0.0215, 0.0238). I pulled get_evidence on object_poses for base1, u_brown, u_orange and line_green over 1793659130.0e9-1793659135.5e9 to characterize what actually happened rather than treat the three crossings as independent small drifts. The trajectories are not independent noise: starting at tf tick 252125013149 (wall_ns ~1793659132297512000) all four objects -- including base1, the bolted fixture that is never picked and had been perfectly static for the entire run up to that tick -- begin moving together, rapidly, over several hundred ms, with positions racing out to tens of centimeters of displacement and z-heights climbing to 0.2-0.4m (e.g. base1 x: 0.404->0.554, u_brown z: 0.044->0.405, u_orange z: 0.044->0.381, line_green z: 0.072->0.389) by 1793659135497492500. A live look() at wall_ns 1793659154571678100 confirms this visually: u_brown, u_orange and line_green are no longer seated in/on the base1 plate, they are seen airborne/displaced above the bench, consistent with a violent separation rather than a slow drift. The mechanism I believe produced this: line_green's prior failed seat left it mis-positioned and ~25 degrees tilted immediately adjacent to base1/u_brown/u_orange; the retry grasp_skill closed on it and the subsequent lift (pick_line_green_retry) dragged/rotated the misaligned part through the other parts and the fixture, and because u_brown-u_orange-u_green-etc and base1-u_brown/u_orange ACM pairs are collision-disabled for planning (not for physics), the resulting interpenetration resolved as a large contact impulse that flung all of them. This is not a mis-arming: three independently-armed, independently-referenced monitors over three different objects crossed together at the same instant, and the pose evidence corroborates the magnitude and timing precisely. All three are genuine non-conformances: base1 (a fixture that must never move) was displaced, and both previously-conformant seated parts u_brown and u_orange were knocked out of their placements by this step, which only named line_green in its object_ids -- u_brown and u_orange were not supposed to be acted on here.

payload.explanation: mon_fccb8146b4c2 (tcp vs line_green, re-armed at the retry grasp close) fired at trigger_wall_ns 1793659135798531800 with triggering_value 0.02005 against threshold 0.02, immediately following the collision/flinging event just recorded under this same step_id (base1/u_brown/u_orange/line_green all displaced together starting ~1793659132.3e9). This is the same physical event continuing: line_green's violent interaction with base1/u_brown/u_orange during the lift evidently also perturbed it relative to the gripper's TCP, marginally exceeding the slip tolerance. I am not treating this as an independent new mechanism -- the evidence already gathered for the collision finding covers the causal story -- but it is recorded as its own clause result because it concerns a different clause (in-hand slippage vs. undisturbed-object) than the three disturbance findings already logged for this step.

payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering steps pick_u_brown through place_approach_line_green_retry. For u_brown and u_orange I independently measured every clause due at their place steps (place_u_brown, place_u_orange) against query_snapshot/get_evidence and found both conformant at the time each place step closed: u_brown seated 0.00215m from u_brown_placement, u_orange seated 0.0022m from u_orange_placement, lift heights, grasp-effort plateaus and width errors all within the registry bounds recorded on those steps, and u_brown's disturbance during u_orange's handling (0.0013m) was within tolerance. line_green's place step (place_line_green) failed on its own evidence: a relative_frame (tcp vs line_green) monitor fired at a 0.02024m departure from its grasp-time reference, and get_evidence showed the object's descent decoupling from the TCP's (object z plateaued at 0.0744 while TCP continued to 0.128) together with a ~25 degree in-hand rotation -- a genuine grasp slip during final insertion, not a mis-arming. The executor's own end_step corroborated this (position_error_m 0.0219 against 0.015 tolerance, orientation_error_deg 25 against 10) -- no disagreement to adjudicate, only confirmation. The executor then attempted an unplanned recovery, pick_line_green_retry (named as unplanned since it is not on the expected process map). During its lift, three independently-armed, independently-referenced stationarity monitors on base1, u_brown and u_orange fired within 1ms of each other, and get_evidence on object_poses showed all four objects (including base1, the bolted fixture that had been static the entire run) beginning to move together at the same tf tick and racing out to tens of centimetres and 0.2-0.4m of z-climb within half a second -- a violent collision/flinging event, which I also confirmed visually with look() showing the parts no longer resting on or in base1. The mechanism I believe produced this: line_green's prior failed, tilted seat left it interpenetrating base1/u_brown/u_orange; the retry grasp and lift dragged it through them, and because their ACM pairs are collision-disabled for planning (not for physics) the resulting contact resolved as a large impulse. The executor itself recognized this at the next begin_step (place_approach_line_green_retry), querying poses before commanding any motion and aborting with 'scene integrity lost' -- an instance of the executor agreeing with WatchDog's evidence after the fact, not a disagreement. At run end (run_ended status=aborted) I independently re-measured every part against its placement frame rather than relying on any earlier flag: u_brown is now 2.963m from u_brown_placement (at world z=-0.754, off the bench entirely), u_orange is 0.3855m off, line_green is 0.3723m off, and base1 itself sits 0.1576m from its run-start reference position -- all catastrophically outside any stated tolerance, and none of this was corrected before the run stopped. inverted_u_yellow was never attempted (object_ids never named it; it remains at its original resting pose), so there is no finding for it, but its absence from the record is moot since the standing violations on u_brown/u_orange/line_green/base1 alone make the end-state non_conformant regardless of completeness. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) remained at their run-start reference poses throughout per their continuously-armed stationarity monitors (no fires), so the collision did not reach them. Verdict: non_conformant -- a violation (multiple, in fact) stands at run end, which outranks incomplete regardless of the executor aborting.
